1	# ALB behind CloudFront (#1345) — CloudFront is the sole public surface
2	# (ADR 0028 §5's api-goes-internal posture, one hop further out). Only the
3	# frontend target group exists; api/worker have no ALB listener and are
4	# reached only via Cloud Map internal DNS (ecs.tf).
5	#
6	# The listener stays plain HTTP :80: TLS terminates at CloudFront (Cognito
7	# requires an HTTPS redirect URI, and there is no custom domain — see
8	# cloudfront.tf). The security group admits only CloudFront's origin-facing
9	# ranges (AWS-managed prefix list), so the ALB is not reachable from an
10	# arbitrary internet address. Those ranges are shared by ALL CloudFront
11	# distributions, so a third party could still origin-point their own
12	# distribution at this ALB's (discoverable) DNS name — which is why the
13	# frontend nginx additionally verifies the X-DataQ-Origin-Secret header our
14	# distribution stamps on every origin fetch (#1355, cloudfront.tf): a foreign
15	# edge doesn't know the secret and gets a 403 for every path except the ALB's
16	# own local health endpoint.
17	
18	# AWS-managed, auto-updated list of CloudFront origin-facing IP ranges.
19	data "aws_ec2_managed_prefix_list" "cloudfront_origin" {
20	  name = "com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing"
21	}
22	
23	resource "aws_security_group" "alb" {
24	  name        = "dataq-app-alb"
25	  description = "ALB - inbound HTTP from CloudFront origin-facing ranges only"
26	  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.app.id
27	
28	  ingress {
29	    description     = "HTTP from CloudFront"
30	    from_port       = 80
31	    to_port         = 80
32	    protocol        = "tcp"
33	    prefix_list_ids = [data.aws_ec2_managed_prefix_list.cloudfront_origin.id]
34	  }
35	
36	  egress {
37	    from_port   = 0
38	    to_port     = 0
39	    protocol    = "-1"
40	    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
41	  }
42	
43	  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-alb" }
44	}
45	
46	resource "aws_lb" "app" {
47	  name               = "dataq-app"
48	  internal           = false
49	  load_balancer_type = "application"
50	  subnets            = aws_subnet.public[*].id
51	  security_groups    = [aws_security_group.alb.id]
52	
53	  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-alb" }
54	}
55	
56	resource "aws_lb_target_group" "frontend" {
57	  name        = "dataq-app-frontend"
58	  port        = 8080
59	  protocol    = "HTTP"
60	  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.app.id
61	  target_type = "ip" # required for Fargate tasks (no EC2 instance id)
62	
63	  health_check {
64	    # /_alb-health — nginx's own local endpoint, exempt from the #1355
65	    # origin-secret guard (the ALB probes the container directly, so it can
66	    # never carry CloudFront's header; probing `/` would 403 and recycle
67	    # healthy tasks once the guard is on). It supersedes the plain `/` chosen
68	    # by #1349 while keeping that fix's property: frontend health means
69	    # "nginx + bundle up", never "the api is up" (nginx PROXIES /healthz to
70	    # the api). Old images without the location fall through to the SPA
71	    # index (200), so the path change deploys safely ahead of the new image.
72	    path                = "/_alb-health"
73	    healthy_threshold   = 2
74	    unhealthy_threshold = 3
75	    interval            = 15
76	    timeout             = 5
77	  }
78	
79	  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-frontend" }
80	}
81	
82	resource "aws_lb_listener" "http" {
83	  load_balancer_arn = aws_lb.app.arn
84	  port              = 80
85	  protocol          = "HTTP"
86	
87	  default_action {
88	    type             = "forward"
89	    target_group_arn = aws_lb_target_group.frontend.arn
90	  }
91	}
92	
93	locals {
94	  # No custom domain yet — CloudFront's own domain is the deployment's public
95	  # HTTPS URL (#1345). Depends only on the distribution (which depends only on
96	  # the ALB), so nothing later in the graph waits on the ECS service itself —
97	  # mirroring the Azure stack's deterministic-FQDN trick that breaks the
98	  # frontend<->api circular dependency.
99	  frontend_url     = "https://${aws_cloudfront_distribution.app.domain_name}"
100	  api_internal_url = "http://api.dataq.local:8000"
101	}
102

1	# CloudFront — the HTTPS front for the ALB (#1345).
2	#
3	# Cognito requires redirect URIs to be HTTPS (http:// is allowed only for
4	# localhost), so the original HTTP-only-ALB design could never complete an
5	# OIDC sign-in. With no custom domain chosen (that decision stands), the
6	# cheapest valid HTTPS origin is CloudFront's own *.cloudfront.net domain with
7	# the default certificate — additive to swap out later: pick a domain, add an
8	# ACM cert + alias here, and the ALB/ECS layers don't change.
9	#
10	# This is a pass-through, not a CDN in anger: the default behavior disables
11	# caching entirely (the app is a dynamic SPA + API; index.html must never be
12	# stale, /api must never be cached) and forwards the full request via the
13	# managed AllViewer policy. Static-asset caching can be added as a dedicated
14	# /assets/* behavior later if it ever matters — nginx already serves
15	# fingerprinted files.
16	
17	data "aws_cloudfront_cache_policy" "caching_disabled" {
18	  name = "Managed-CachingDisabled"
19	}
20	
21	data "aws_cloudfront_origin_request_policy" "all_viewer" {
22	  name = "Managed-AllViewer"
23	}
24	
25	resource "aws_cloudfront_distribution" "app" {
26	  enabled         = true
27	  comment         = "DataQ frontend — HTTPS front for the ALB (no custom domain)"
28	  is_ipv6_enabled = true
29	  # Cheapest edge-location class (NA + EU) — this is an HTTPS terminator, not
30	  # a latency play.
31	  price_class = "PriceClass_100"
32	
33	  origin {
34	    domain_name = aws_lb.app.dns_name
35	    origin_id   = "alb"
36	
37	    # Origin secret (#1355): stamped on every origin fetch and verified by the
38	    # frontend nginx (DATAQ_ORIGIN_SECRET) — closes the residual gap alb.tf
39	    # documents, where a third party's OWN distribution could origin-point at
40	    # this ALB's discoverable DNS name through the shared CloudFront
41	    # origin-facing ranges. CloudFront overwrites any viewer-sent header of
42	    # the same name, so the value can't be probed through this distribution.
43	    # (Visible in the distribution config to anyone with CloudFront read
44	    # access — an origin-authentication token, not a user credential.)
45	    #
46	    # Residual, stated honestly (#1378 review): the edge→origin hop is plain
47	    # HTTP (origin_protocol_policy http-only — no custom domain means no cert
48	    # the ALB could serve), so the header transits that leg in cleartext. An
49	    # on-path observer of AWS's edge→ALB path could read it; that adversary
50	    # class already sees the whole session traffic on the same hop. Closing
51	    # it = custom domain + ACM on the ALB + https-only, the documented
52	    # follow-up in the README's known-gaps list.
53	    custom_header {
54	      name  = "X-DataQ-Origin-Secret"
55	      value = random_password.origin_secret.result
56	    }
57	
58	    custom_origin_config {
59	      http_port  = 80
60	      https_port = 443
61	      # The ALB listener is plain HTTP :80; TLS terminates at CloudFront. The
62	      # ALB's security group admits only CloudFront's origin-facing address
63	      # ranges (alb.tf) — see that file's note on what that does and does not
64	      # guarantee (#1355).
65	      origin_protocol_policy = "http-only"
66	      origin_ssl_protocols   = ["TLSv1.2"]
67	      # Long warehouse-bound API calls (column profiler, dry-run, test-
68	      # connection against a cold warehouse) routinely exceed CloudFront's 30s
69	      # default; match the ALB's 60s idle timeout so CloudFront isn't the
70	      # tightest hop (/code-review finding).
71	      origin_read_timeout      = 60
72	      origin_keepalive_timeout = 60
73	    }
74	  }
75	
76	  default_cache_behavior {
77	    target_origin_id       = "alb"
78	    viewer_protocol_policy = "redirect-to-https"
79	    allowed_methods        = ["GET", "HEAD", "OPTIONS", "PUT", "POST", "PATCH", "DELETE"]
80	    cached_methods         = ["GET", "HEAD"]
81	    compress               = true
82	
83	    cache_policy_id          = data.aws_cloudfront_cache_policy.caching_disabled.id
84	    origin_request_policy_id = data.aws_cloudfront_origin_request_policy.all_viewer.id
85	  }
86	
87	  restrictions {
88	    geo_restriction {
89	      restriction_type = "none"
90	    }
91	  }
92	
93	  viewer_certificate {
94	    cloudfront_default_certificate = true
95	  }
96	
97	  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-cloudfront" }
98	}
99	
100	# Alphanumeric only (`special = false`): the nginx guard's map key uses ":" as
101	# its delimiter and the value must stay free of nginx map metacharacters.
102	resource "random_password" "origin_secret" {
103	  length  = 40
104	  special = false
105	}
106	
107	# Injected into the frontend task via the `secrets` block (execution-role read,
108	# same pattern as database-url/redis-url) rather than plaintext task-def env.
109	resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret" "origin_secret" {
110	  name                    = "dataq-app-infra/origin-secret"
111	  recovery_window_in_days = 0
112	}
113	
114	resource "aws_secretsmanager_secret_version" "origin_secret" {
115	  secret_id     = aws_secretsmanager_secret.origin_secret.id
116	  secret_string = random_password.origin_secret.result
117	}
118

1	# ECS Fargate — api (internal, Cloud Map DNS), worker (Celery + embedded
2	# beat, min=max=1 desired count — mirrors the Azure Container App's
3	# min_replicas=1 rationale: it can't scale to zero because it runs beat), and
4	# frontend (public via the ALB). All three run images from GHCR (public,
5	# anonymous pull — ADR 0023), same as the Azure stack.
6	
7	resource "aws_ecs_cluster" "app" {
8	  name = "dataq-app"
9	
10	  tags = { Name = "dataq-app" }
11	}
12	
13	# One shared security group for every ECS task: self-referencing ingress lets
14	# api/worker/frontend talk to each other (and to Redis/RDS, which have their
15	# own SGs allowing traffic FROM this one), plus a narrow allow from the ALB
16	# SG for the frontend's published port.
17	resource "aws_security_group" "ecs_tasks" {
18	  name = "dataq-app-ecs-tasks"
19	  # EC2 SG descriptions allow ONLY a-zA-Z0-9. _-:/()#,@[]+=&;{}!$* (#1357) —
20	  # no em-dash, and no '>' either (the first fix missed that).
21	  description = "DataQ ECS tasks - internal task-to-task traffic + ALB to frontend"
22	  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.app.id
23	
24	  egress {
25	    from_port   = 0
26	    to_port     = 0
27	    protocol    = "-1"
28	    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
29	  }
30	
31	  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-ecs-tasks" }
32	}
33	
34	resource "aws_security_group_rule" "ecs_tasks_self_ingress" {
35	  # Narrower than "every port" on purpose: the only task-to-task call within
36	  # this security group is frontend -> api on 8000 (Cloud Map DNS). worker
37	  # and frontend serve nothing another task calls, so opening the full
38	  # 0-65535 range would grant blast-radius no actual traffic pattern needs.
39	  type                     = "ingress"
40	  from_port                = 8000
41	  to_port                  = 8000
42	  protocol                 = "tcp"
43	  security_group_id        = aws_security_group.ecs_tasks.id
44	  source_security_group_id = aws_security_group.ecs_tasks.id
45	}
46	
47	resource "aws_security_group_rule" "ecs_tasks_from_alb" {
48	  type                     = "ingress"
49	  from_port                = 8080
50	  to_port                  = 8080
51	  protocol                 = "tcp"
52	  security_group_id        = aws_security_group.ecs_tasks.id
53	  source_security_group_id = aws_security_group.alb.id
54	}
55	
56	# Cloud Map private DNS namespace — how the frontend reaches the api
57	# internally (DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM=http://api.dataq.local:8000, alb.tf's
58	# local.api_internal_url), the same role the Azure environment's
59	# `.internal.<domain>` FQDN plays there.
60	resource "aws_service_discovery_private_dns_namespace" "app" {
61	  name = "dataq.local"
62	  vpc  = aws_vpc.app.id
63	}
64	
65	resource "aws_service_discovery_service" "api" {
66	  name = "api"
67	
68	  dns_config {
69	    namespace_id = aws_service_discovery_private_dns_namespace.app.id
70	    dns_records {
71	      type = "A"
72	      ttl  = 10
73	    }
74	  }
75	
76	  health_check_custom_config {
77	    failure_threshold = 1
78	  }
79	}
80	
81	locals {
82	  backend_image  = "${var.backend_image_repo}:${var.image_tag}"
83	  frontend_image = "${var.frontend_image_repo}:${var.frontend_image_tag}"
84	
85	  # Non-secret env, shared by api + worker — mirrors containerapps.tf's
86	  # local.app_env, with AWS-shaped values in place of the Azure ones.
87	  app_env = [
88	    { name = "ENVIRONMENT", value = var.environment },
89	    { name = "LOG_LEVEL", value = "INFO" },
90	    { name = "SAMPLE_FAILURES_RETENTION_DAYS", value = "30" },
91	    # Runtime SecretStore -> AWS Secrets Manager via the ECS task role (no
92	    # bootstrap credential to hold — same "no credential at all" posture the
93	    # Azure UAMI + Key Vault pairing has).
94	    { name = "SECRET_STORE", value = "aws_secrets_manager" },
95	    { name = "AWS_SECRETS_MANAGER_PREFIX", value = "${var.aws_secrets_manager_prefix}/" },
96	    # Real auth in prod (AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=false) via the generic OIDC path
97	    # (ADR 0026 amendment) — NOT the Azure fields, which stay unset.
98	    { name = "AUTH_DEV_BYPASS", value = "false" },
99	    { name = "OIDC_ISSUER", value = local.cognito_issuer },
100	    { name = "OIDC_AUDIENCE", value = aws_cognito_user_pool_client.spa.id },
101	    { name = "WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS", value = var.workspace_admin_emails },
102	    # Rate-limit per-IP keying (ADR 0035). Three proxies append to
103	    # X-Forwarded-For on the way in — CloudFront (appends the viewer IP), the
104	    # ALB (appends CloudFront's edge IP), and the frontend nginx
105	    # ($proxy_add_x_forwarded_for appends the ALB IP) — so the real client is
106	    # 3 entries from the right, same depth as the Azure stack's
107	    # envoy+nginx+envoy chain. Confirm against one logged live XFF
108	    # post-deploy, same as the Azure note.
109	    { name = "RATE_LIMIT_XFF_TRUSTED_HOPS", value = "3" },
110	    { name = "CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS", value = "" },
111	    { name = "PUBLIC_BASE_URL", value = local.frontend_url },
112	    { name = "ADF_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME", value = "adf-webhook-secret" },
113	    { name = "AIRFLOW_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME", value = "airflow-webhook-secret" },
114	    { name = "DBT_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME", value = "dbt-webhook-secret" },
115	    { name = "SLACK_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME", value = "channel-slack-webhook" },
116	    # Spans + OTel logs → the ADOT sidecar on task-local loopback (#1369,
117	    # adot.tf) → X-Ray / CloudWatch. The app half is the vendor-neutral
118	    # core/otel.py (#589); this is just where its OTLP consumer lives.
119	    { name = "OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT", value = "http://localhost:4318" },
120	    # Email alert channel via SES (#1368, ses.tf) — everything derives from
121	    # var.alert_email; empty leaves the channel off (config.py's gate). The
122	    # SMTP password lives at dataq/channel-email-password in Secrets Manager,
123	    # read through the app's own SecretStore at send time.
124	    { name = "EMAIL_SMTP_HOST", value = local.ses_smtp_host },
125	    { name = "EMAIL_SMTP_PORT", value = "587" },
126	    { name = "EMAIL_PASSWORD_SECRET_NAME", value = "channel-email-password" },
127	    { name = "EMAIL_USERNAME", value = local.email_username },
128	    { name = "EMAIL_FROM", value = var.alert_email },
129	    { name = "EMAIL_TO", value = local.alert_email_to },
130	  ]
131	
132	  worker_env = concat(local.app_env, [
133	    { name = "WAREHOUSE_LINEAGE_ENABLED", value = "true" },
134	  ])
135	
136	  # Boot-critical secrets, injected via the task definition's `secrets` block
137	  # (execution-role-read from the infra-owned Secrets Manager entries) —
138	  # mirrors the Azure stack's inline-Container-App-secret pattern; same
139	  # reasoning (decouple first-revision activation from any IAM-propagation
140	  # delay on the app's OWN Secrets Manager grant).
141	  boot_secrets = [
142	    { name = "DATABASE_URL", valueFrom = aws_secretsmanager_secret.database_url.arn },
143	    { name = "REDIS_URL", valueFrom = aws_secretsmanager_secret.redis_url.arn },
144	  ]
145	}
146	
147	# ── API (internal, Cloud Map) ────────────────────────────────────────────
148	
149	resource "aws_ecs_task_definition" "api" {
150	  family                   = "dataq-app-api"
151	  requires_compatibilities = ["FARGATE"]
152	  network_mode             = "awsvpc"
153	  cpu                      = 512
154	  memory                   = 1024
155	  execution_role_arn       = aws_iam_role.ecs_task_execution.arn
156	  task_role_arn            = aws_iam_role.ecs_task_api.arn
157	
158	  container_definitions = jsonencode([
159	    {
160	      name         = "api"
161	      image        = local.backend_image
162	      essential    = true
163	      portMappings = [{ containerPort = 8000, protocol = "tcp" }]
164	      environment  = local.app_env
165	      secrets      = local.boot_secrets
166	      logConfiguration = {
167	        logDriver = "awslogs"
168	        options = {
169	          "awslogs-group"         = aws_cloudwatch_log_group.api.name
170	          "awslogs-region"        = var.aws_region
171	          "awslogs-stream-prefix" = "api"
172	        }
173	      }
174	    },
175	    # ADOT collector sidecar (#1369, adot.tf) — OTLP in on localhost:4318,
176	    # traces → X-Ray, OTel logs → CloudWatch. NOTE ignore_changes below:
177	    # adding/changing this on a LIVE stack needs `tofu apply -replace` on this
178	    # task definition + an `update-service` to the new revision (README,
179	    # "Rolling task-definition changes").
180	    local.adot_container["api"],
181	  ])
182	
183	  # CI rolls the live image out-of-band (new task-def revision via
184	  # `aws ecs register-task-definition` + `update-service`) — mirrors the
185	  # Azure stack's `ignore_changes` on the container image, same reasoning.
186	  lifecycle {
187	    ignore_changes = [container_definitions]
188	  }
189	
190	  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-api" }
191	}
192	
193	resource "aws_ecs_service" "api" {
194	  name            = "dataq-app-api"
195	  cluster         = aws_ecs_cluster.app.id
196	  task_definition = aws_ecs_task_definition.api.arn
197	  desired_count   = 1
198	  launch_type     = "FARGATE"
199	
200	  network_configuration {
201	    subnets          = aws_subnet.public[*].id
202	    security_groups  = [aws_security_group.ecs_tasks.id]
203	    assign_public_ip = true # no NAT — see main.tf's decision note
204	  }
205	
206	  service_registries {
207	    registry_arn = aws_service_discovery_service.api.arn
208	  }
209	
210	  lifecycle {
211	    ignore_changes = [task_definition]
212	  }
213	}
214	
215	# ── Worker (Celery worker + embedded beat) ──────────────────────────────
216	
217	resource "aws_ecs_task_definition" "worker" {
218	  family                   = "dataq-app-worker"
219	  requires_compatibilities = ["FARGATE"]
220	  network_mode             = "awsvpc"
221	  cpu                      = 1024
222	  memory                   = 2048
223	  execution_role_arn       = aws_iam_role.ecs_task_execution.arn
224	  task_role_arn            = aws_iam_role.ecs_task_worker.arn
225	
226	  container_definitions = jsonencode([
227	    {
228	      name        = "worker"
229	      image       = local.backend_image
230	      essential   = true
231	      command     = ["celery", "-A", "backend.app.worker.celery_app", "worker", "-B", "--loglevel=INFO"]
232	      environment = local.worker_env
233	      secrets     = local.boot_secrets
234	      logConfiguration = {
235	        logDriver = "awslogs"
236	        options = {
237	          "awslogs-group"         = aws_cloudwatch_log_group.worker.name
238	          "awslogs-region"        = var.aws_region
239	          "awslogs-stream-prefix" = "worker"
240	        }
241	      }
242	    },
243	    # Same ADOT sidecar + same -replace rollout note as the api task def.
244	    local.adot_container["worker"],
245	  ])
246	
247	  lifecycle {
248	    ignore_changes = [container_definitions]
249	  }
250	
251	  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-worker" }
252	}
253	
254	resource "aws_ecs_service" "worker" {
255	  name            = "dataq-app-worker"
256	  cluster         = aws_ecs_cluster.app.id
257	  task_definition = aws_ecs_task_definition.worker.arn
258	  # Cannot scale to zero — runs embedded celery-beat (schedule dispatcher +
259	  # orchestration polling), same as the Azure Container App's min_replicas=1.
260	  desired_count = 1
261	  launch_type   = "FARGATE"
262	
263	  network_configuration {
264	    subnets          = aws_subnet.public[*].id
265	    security_groups  = [aws_security_group.ecs_tasks.id]
266	    assign_public_ip = true
267	  }
268	
269	  lifecycle {
270	    ignore_changes = [task_definition]
271	  }
272	}
273	
274	# ── Frontend (nginx SPA, sole public surface) ───────────────────────────
275	
276	resource "aws_ecs_task_definition" "frontend" {
277	  family                   = "dataq-app-frontend"
278	  requires_compatibilities = ["FARGATE"]
279	  network_mode             = "awsvpc"
280	  cpu                      = 256
281	  memory                   = 512
282	  execution_role_arn       = aws_iam_role.ecs_task_execution.arn
283	
284	  container_definitions = jsonencode([
285	    {
286	      name         = "frontend"
287	      image        = local.frontend_image
288	      essential    = true
289	      portMappings = [{ containerPort = 8080, protocol = "tcp" }]
290	      environment = [
291	        { name = "DATAQ_API_UPSTREAM", value = local.api_internal_url },
292	        { name = "DATAQ_AUTH_MODE", value = "oidc" },
293	        { name = "DATAQ_AUTH_AUTHORITY", value = local.cognito_issuer },
294	        { name = "DATAQ_AUTH_CLIENT_ID", value = aws_cognito_user_pool_client.spa.id },
295	        # Scope override (#1347): Cognito has no offline_access scope and errors
296	        # (invalid_scope) on the SPA's default list; refresh tokens are issued
297	        # on the code grant regardless. Must match cognito.tf's
298	        # allowed_oauth_scopes.
299	        { name = "DATAQ_AUTH_SCOPE", value = "openid email profile" },
300	        # Sign-out dialect (#1364): Cognito's /logout is not RP-Initiated-Logout-
301	        # conformant — it needs client_id + logout_uri and 400s on the standard
302	        # id_token_hint/post_logout_redirect_uri, stranding the user on a raw
303	        # "Client does not exist" error page with the hosted-UI session alive.
304	        { name = "DATAQ_AUTH_LOGOUT_STYLE", value = "cognito" },
305	      ]
306	      # Origin-secret guard (#1355): nginx 403s any request not carrying the
307	      # header CloudFront stamps on origin fetches (cloudfront.tf). Injected
308	      # as a secret, not plaintext env. NOTE ignore_changes below: on a LIVE
309	      # stack a plain apply never registers this — roll it with
310	      # `tofu apply -replace` on this task definition + `update-service`
311	      # (README, "Rolling task-definition changes"), or the guard silently
312	      # stays fail-open while CloudFront stamps a header nobody checks.
313	      secrets = [
314	        { name = "DATAQ_ORIGIN_SECRET", valueFrom = aws_secretsmanager_secret.origin_secret.arn },
315	      ]
316	      logConfiguration = {
317	        logDriver = "awslogs"
318	        options = {
319	          "awslogs-group"         = aws_cloudwatch_log_group.frontend.name
320	          "awslogs-region"        = var.aws_region
321	          "awslogs-stream-prefix" = "frontend"
322	        }
323	      }
324	    }
325	  ])
326	
327	  lifecycle {
328	    ignore_changes = [container_definitions]
329	  }
330	
331	  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-frontend" }
332	}
333	
334	resource "aws_ecs_service" "frontend" {
335	  name            = "dataq-app-frontend"
336	  cluster         = aws_ecs_cluster.app.id
337	  task_definition = aws_ecs_task_definition.frontend.arn
338	  desired_count   = 1
339	  launch_type     = "FARGATE"
340	
341	  network_configuration {
342	    subnets          = aws_subnet.public[*].id
343	    security_groups  = [aws_security_group.ecs_tasks.id]
344	    assign_public_ip = true
345	  }
346	
347	  load_balancer {
348	    target_group_arn = aws_lb_target_group.frontend.arn
349	    container_name   = "frontend"
350	    container_port   = 8080
351	  }
352	
353	  lifecycle {
354	    ignore_changes = [task_definition]
355	  }
356	
357	  depends_on = [aws_lb_listener.http]
358	}

1	# RDS PostgreSQL — the app's own instance (this account is dedicated to this
2	# deployment, so unlike Azure's shared-server pattern there's no sibling
3	# harness stack to coordinate with).
4	
5	resource "aws_db_subnet_group" "app" {
6	  name       = "dataq-app-db"
7	  subnet_ids = aws_subnet.public[*].id
8	}
9

11	  name        = "dataq-app-rds"
12	  description = "Postgres - inbound only from the ECS tasks security group"
13	  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.app.id
14	
15	  ingress {
16	    description     = "Postgres from ECS tasks"
17	    from_port       = 5432
18	    to_port         = 5432
19	    protocol        = "tcp"
20	    security_groups = [aws_security_group.ecs_tasks.id]
21	  }
22	
23	  egress {
24	    from_port   = 0
25	    to_port     = 0
26	    protocol    = "-1"
27	    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
28	  }
29	
30	  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-rds" }
31	}
32	
33	resource "aws_db_instance" "app" {
34	  identifier     = "dataq-app"
35	  engine         = "postgres"
36	  engine_version = "16"
37	  instance_class = "db.t4g.micro"
38	
39	  allocated_storage     = 20
40	  max_allocated_storage = 100
41	  storage_type          = "gp3"
42	  storage_encrypted     = true
43	
44	  db_name  = var.app_db_name
45	  username = var.app_db_user
46	  password = var.app_db_password
47	
48	  db_subnet_group_name   = aws_db_subnet_group.app.name
49	  vpc_security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.rds.id]
50	  # Not in a NAT'd private subnet (see main.tf's decision note) — kept
51	  # unreachable from the internet by NOT setting a public IP, independent of
52	  # the subnet's own IGW route.
53	  publicly_accessible = false
54	
55	  # Bring-up posture, mirrors the Azure stack's key_vault_purge_protection
56	  # default — flip these once this becomes a durable deployment.
57	  skip_final_snapshot     = true
58	  deletion_protection     = false
59	  backup_retention_period = 1
60	
61	  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-db" }
62	}
63	
64	locals {
65	  # sslmode=require: RDS enforces TLS by default. urlencode() avoids a
66	  # DSN-breaking special character in the password, same as the Azure stack.
67	  database_url = "REDACTED"
68	}

1	# ElastiCache Redis — AWS-native managed Redis for the Celery broker + rate
2	# limits (ADR 0035). Decision: managed ElastiCache, not self-hosted-on-Fargate
3	# like the Azure stack's Redis Container App — the user's explicit choice for
4	# the AWS deployment (see the approved plan's cost note: a few dollars/month
5	# more than self-hosting, ongoing).
6	#
7	# aws_elasticache_replication_group (not aws_elasticache_cluster): the
8	# replication-group resource is what actually supports auth_token +
9	# transit_encryption_enabled cleanly. One node, no read replica — this is a
10	# single Celery broker, not a fan-out cache.
11	
12	resource "aws_elasticache_subnet_group" "app" {
13	  name       = "dataq-app-redis"
14	  subnet_ids = aws_subnet.public[*].id
15	}
16	
17	resource "aws_security_group" "redis" {
18	  name        = "dataq-app-redis"
19	  description = "Redis - inbound only from the ECS tasks security group"
20	  vpc_id      = aws_vpc.app.id
21	
22	  ingress {
23	    description     = "Redis from ECS tasks"
24	    from_port       = 6379
25	    to_port         = 6379
26	    protocol        = "tcp"
27	    security_groups = [aws_security_group.ecs_tasks.id]
28	  }
29	
30	  egress {
31	    from_port   = 0
32	    to_port     = 0
33	    protocol    = "-1"
34	    cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"]
35	  }
36	
37	  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-redis" }
38	}
39	
40	# ElastiCache auth_token: 16-128 printable ASCII chars, excluding '/', '"',
41	# '@'. `special = false` sidesteps the excluded-character set entirely rather
42	# than trying to allow-list a safe subset.
43	resource "random_password" "redis_auth" {
44	  length  = 32
45	  special = false
46	}
47	
48	resource "aws_elasticache_replication_group" "app" {
49	  replication_group_id = "dataq-app"
50	  description          = "DataQ Celery broker + rate-limit store"
51	  engine               = "redis"
52	  engine_version       = "7.1"
53	  node_type            = "cache.t4g.micro"
54	  num_cache_clusters   = 1
55	  port                 = 6379
56	
57	  subnet_group_name  = aws_elasticache_subnet_group.app.name
58	  security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.redis.id]
59	
60	  # TLS + password required together — same defense-in-depth posture as the
61	  # Azure stack's self-hosted Redis (--requirepass over an internal-only
62	  # ingress). transit_encryption_enabled is what makes auth_token usable at
63	  # all on this resource.
64	  transit_encryption_enabled = true
65	  auth_token                 = random_password.redis_auth.result
66	
67	  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-redis" }
68	}
69	
70	locals {
71	  # rediss:// (TLS) scheme — transit_encryption_enabled requires TLS
72	  # connections; redis-py/celery both understand the scheme.
73	  #
74	  # ssl_cert_reqs=required is MANDATORY, not belt-and-braces (#1361): celery's
75	  # redis result backend raises ValueError on any rediss:// URL that omits the
76	  # parameter, so without it the worker crash-loops at boot and the api's
77	  # producer dies on first dispatch. Lowercase `required` is the one spelling
78	  # all three consumers accept (celery 5.6.3 → ssl.CERT_REQUIRED, redis-py
79	  # 5.3.1 from_url, kombu 5.6.2), and ElastiCache serves an Amazon-CA cert so
80	  # full verification works against system CAs.
81	  redis_url = "REDACTED"
82	}

1	# The DataQ backend on Container Apps — api (external ingress), worker (Celery +
2	# embedded beat), and the migrate Job. All three run the SAME GHCR image
3	# (ghcr.io/theurgicduke771/dataq-backend:<tag>), pulled anonymously (public
4	# package, ADR 0023 — no registry block / credential).
5	#
6	# Boot-critical secrets (DATABASE_URL, App Insights) are inline Container App
7	# secrets, NOT KV references (see keyvault.tf for why). REDIS_URL is non-secret
8	# (in-environment, no auth). The app's runtime SecretStore reads datasource creds
9	# from Key Vault via the attached user-assigned identity (SECRET_STORE +
10	# AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL).
11	
12	locals {
13	  backend_image   = "${var.backend_image_repo}:${var.image_tag}"
14	  azure_tenant_id = var.azure_tenant_id != "" ? var.azure_tenant_id : data.azurerm_client_config.current.tenant_id
15	
16	  # Inline secrets shared by api + worker (+ DATABASE_URL also on the migrate job).
17	  app_secrets = [
18	    { name = "database-url", value = local.database_url },
19	    { name = "redis-url", value = local.redis_url },
20	    { name = "appinsights-conn", value = azurerm_application_insights.app.connection_string },
21	  ]
22	
23	  # Non-secret env + secret_name references, shared by api + worker.
24	  app_env = [
25	    { name = "ENVIRONMENT", value = var.environment },
26	    { name = "LOG_LEVEL", value = "INFO" },
27	    { name = "DATABASE_URL", secret_name = "database-url" },
28	    { name = "REDIS_URL", secret_name = "redis-url" },
29	    { name = "APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING", secret_name = "appinsights-conn" },
30	    { name = "SAMPLE_FAILURES_RETENTION_DAYS", value = "30" },
31	    # Runtime SecretStore -> Key Vault via the user-assigned identity.
32	    { name = "SECRET_STORE", value = "azure_key_vault" },
33	    { name = "AZURE_KEY_VAULT_URL", value = azurerm_key_vault.app.vault_uri },
34	    # DefaultAzureCredential can't select a USER-assigned identity without being
35	    # told which one. Without this, every Key Vault read fails (no MI chosen) —
36	    # breaking secret resolution for connection tests, suite runs, and the
37	    # orchestration poll (#406). Must be the UAMI's client id, not principal id.
38	    { name = "AZURE_CLIENT_ID", value = azurerm_user_assigned_identity.app.client_id },
39	    # Real SSO in prod (AUTH_DEV_BYPASS=false). Client IDs come from the SSO app
40	    # registrations created in sso.tf; init_auth() validates v2 tokens against
41	    # AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID + AZURE_TENANT_ID.
42	    { name = "AUTH_DEV_BYPASS", value = "false" },
43	    { name = "AZURE_TENANT_ID", value = local.azure_tenant_id },
44	    { name = "AZURE_API_CLIENT_ID", value = azuread_application.api.client_id },
45	    { name = "AZURE_SPA_CLIENT_ID", value = azuread_application.spa.client_id },
46	    { name = "AZURE_API_SCOPE", value = var.azure_api_scope },
47	    # Guest (B2B / external) sign-in. Off by default (secure); this deployment
48	    # opts in via tfvars because the owner signs in with a guest account. When
49	    # off, the token validator rejects guests with 403 "Guest users not allowed".
50	    { name = "AZURE_ALLOW_GUEST_USERS", value = var.azure_allow_guest_users ? "true" : "false" },
51	    { name = "WORKSPACE_ADMIN_EMAILS", value = var.workspace_admin_emails },
52	    # Rate-limit per-IP keying (ADR 0035). The measured prod ingress chain is
53	    # public-envoy + nginx + internal-envoy = 3 XFF appends, so the real client
54	    # is the 3rd entry from the right; the default of 1 (rightmost) would collapse
55	    # every client into the shared nginx-pod IP. Confirm the exact depth against
56	    # one logged live XFF post-deploy.
57	    { name = "RATE_LIMIT_XFF_TRUSTED_HOPS", value = "3" },
58	    # Empty: the frontend Container App proxies /api same-origin (nginx), so the
59	    # FastAPI CORS middleware stays off (README §4 / ADR 0018 / ADR 0028).
60	    { name = "CORS_ALLOW_ORIGINS", value = "" },
61	    # Public origin for the inbound-webhook URLs the admin webhook-config surface
62	    # generates (#490). The frontend host proxies /api same-origin, so an
63	    # orchestrator POSTing to <frontend>/api/v1/orchestration/events/... reaches
64	    # the api. Computed from the env domain (local.frontend_url) — not a reference
65	    # to the frontend resource — so api + frontend don't form a dependency cycle.
66	    { name = "PUBLIC_BASE_URL", value = local.frontend_url },
67	    # Webhook secret KEY names (values live in Key Vault — keyvault.tf).
68	    { name = "ADF_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME", value = "adf-webhook-secret" },
69	    { name = "AIRFLOW_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME", value = "airflow-webhook-secret" },
70	    { name = "DBT_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME", value = "dbt-webhook-secret" },
71	    # Alerting channels (Slack + email) behind the ResultPublisher composite.
72	    # Secret NAMES point at Key Vault (the webhook URL / app-password live there);
73	    # SMTP coordinates are non-secret. Each publisher self-no-ops until its secret
74	    # + (for email) recipients are set, so leaving the email_* vars empty = email
75	    # off. Email addresses come from the gitignored tfvars (PII, not in git).
76	    { name = "SLACK_WEBHOOK_SECRET_NAME", value = "channel-slack-webhook" },
77	    { name = "EMAIL_SMTP_HOST", value = "smtp.gmail.com" },
78	    { name = "EMAIL_SMTP_PORT", value = "587" },
79	    { name = "EMAIL_PASSWORD_SECRET_NAME", value = "channel-email-password" },
80	    { name = "EMAIL_USERNAME", value = var.email_username },
81	    { name = "EMAIL_FROM", value = var.email_from },
82	    { name = "EMAIL_TO", value = var.email_to },
83	  ]
84	
85	  # Worker-only env, on top of app_env.
86	  #
87	  # WAREHOUSE_LINEAGE_ENABLED gates the daily `refresh_warehouse_lineage` beat task
88	  # (#858, ADR 0034). The backend default is `warehouse_lineage_enabled: bool = False`
89	  # ("dark by default" — the ACCOUNT_USAGE / system.access views it reads need a grant
90	  # the connection principal may not hold), so the sweep runs ONLY while this is set.
91	  #
92	  # Adopted into IaC by #1086: it was live on prod but absent from this stack, so any
93	  # apply — for any unrelated reason — would have deleted it and silently stopped
94	  # warehouse lineage. Worker-only because only the worker runs beat.
95	  worker_env = concat(local.app_env, [
96	    { name = "WAREHOUSE_LINEAGE_ENABLED", value = "true" },
97	  ])
98	}
99	
100	# ── API (FastAPI, external ingress) ──────────────────────────────────────────
101	resource "azurerm_container_app" "api" {
102	  name                         = "dataq-app-api"
103	  container_app_environment_id = data.azurerm_container_app_environment.shared.id
104	  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name
105	  revision_mode                = "Single"
106	
107	  identity {
108	    type         = "UserAssigned"
109	    identity_ids = [azurerm_user_assigned_identity.app.id]
110	  }
111	
112	  dynamic "secret" {
113	    for_each = local.app_secrets
114	    content {
115	      name  = secret.value.name
116	      value = secret.value.value
117	    }
118	  }
119	
120	  # INTERNAL ingress (ADR 0028 §5): the frontend Container App is the sole public
121	  # surface and reverse-proxies /api + /mcp to this app over the in-environment
122	  # endpoint. Not externally reachable — direct internet calls to the api are gone,
123	  # and in-env frontend->api traffic no longer hairpins out to a public FQDN.
124	  # External orchestrator webhooks (ADF/Airflow) still reach the api: they POST to
125	  # the public frontend (PUBLIC_BASE_URL), which proxies the path through.
126	  ingress {
127	    external_enabled = false
128	    target_port      = 8000
129	    transport        = "auto"
130	    # Accept plain HTTP on the internal endpoint. ACA's internal service-to-service
131	    # pattern is HTTP (local.api_internal_url is http://); with this off, ACA
132	    # redirects port-80 requests to 443, which surfaces to the frontend nginx proxy
133	    # as HTTP 426 "Upgrade Required" and breaks every /api call. Safe here: the api
134	    # is internal-only (external_enabled=false), so this traffic never leaves the
135	    # Container Apps environment.
136	    allow_insecure_connections = true
137	    traffic_weight {
138	      latest_revision = true
139	      percentage      = 100
140	    }
141	  }
142	
143	  template {
144	    min_replicas = 1
145	    max_replicas = 3
146	    container {
147	      name   = "api"
148	      image  = local.backend_image
149	      cpu    = 0.5
150	      memory = "1Gi"
151	      # Image CMD already runs `uvicorn backend.app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0
152	      # --port 8000` (no --reload in the image), so no command override.
153	      dynamic "env" {
154	        for_each = local.app_env
155	        content {
156	          name        = env.value.name
157	          value       = lookup(env.value, "value", null)
158	          secret_name = lookup(env.value, "secret_name", null)
159	        }
160	      }
161	    }
162	  }
163	
164	  # The Deploy workflow rolls images out-of-band (`az containerapp update
165	  # --image <sha>`), so the live image is ahead of var.image_tag. Ignore the image
166	  # here or every `terraform apply` would roll prod BACK to var.image_tag. The
167	  # workflow is the image source of truth; Terraform owns the rest of the app.
168	  lifecycle {
169	    ignore_changes = [template[0].container[0].image]
170	  }
171	
172	  tags       = local.common_tags
173	  depends_on = [azurerm_role_assignment.kv_app_secrets]
174	}
175	
176	# ── Worker (Celery worker + embedded beat) ───────────────────────────────────
177	resource "azurerm_container_app" "worker" {
178	  name                         = "dataq-app-worker"
179	  container_app_environment_id = data.azurerm_container_app_environment.shared.id
180	  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name
181	  revision_mode                = "Single"
182	
183	  identity {
184	    type         = "UserAssigned"
185	    identity_ids = [azurerm_user_assigned_identity.app.id]
186	  }
187	
188	  dynamic "secret" {
189	    for_each = local.app_secrets
190	    content {
191	      name  = secret.value.name
192	      value = secret.value.value
193	    }
194	  }
195	
196	  template {
197	    # min_replicas = 1: the worker also runs celery-beat (-B) for the schedule
198	    # dispatcher + orchestration polling, so it can't scale to zero.
199	    min_replicas = 1
200	    max_replicas = 1
201	    container {
202	      name    = "worker"
203	      image   = local.backend_image
204	      cpu     = 1.0
205	      memory  = "2Gi"
206	      command = ["celery", "-A", "backend.app.worker.celery_app", "worker", "-B", "--loglevel=INFO"]
207	      dynamic "env" {
208	        for_each = local.worker_env
209	        content {
210	          name        = env.value.name
211	          value       = lookup(env.value, "value", null)
212	          secret_name = lookup(env.value, "secret_name", null)
213	        }
214	      }
215	    }
216	  }
217	
218	  # Image is workflow-managed (see the api resource) — ignore it so an apply never
219	  # rolls the worker back to var.image_tag.
220	  lifecycle {
221	    ignore_changes = [template[0].container[0].image]
222	  }
223	
224	  tags       = local.common_tags
225	  depends_on = [azurerm_role_assignment.kv_app_secrets]
226	}
227	
228	# ── Migrate Job (alembic upgrade head) ───────────────────────────────────────
229	# Manual-trigger job the Deploy workflow runs BEFORE rolling the apps (additive,
230	# backward-compatible migrations — CLAUDE.md). alembic.ini's script_location is
231	# relative to backend/, so cd there first (mirrors docker-compose's migrate svc).
232	resource "azurerm_container_app_job" "migrate" {
233	  name                         = "dataq-app-migrate"
234	  container_app_environment_id = data.azurerm_container_app_environment.shared.id
235	  resource_group_name          = data.azurerm_resource_group.dataq.name
236	  # A Container Apps Job must be in the same region as its (shared) environment.
237	  location = data.azurerm_container_app_environment.shared.location
238	
239	  replica_timeout_in_seconds = 900
240	  replica_retry_limit        = 1
241	
242	  manual_trigger_config {
243	    parallelism              = 1
244	    replica_completion_count = 1
245	  }

14	# firewall rule (the apps are Azure services), same as airflow.

17	# PostgreSQL's referential-integrity check switches to the REFERENCED TABLE'S OWNER
18	# before invoking an implicit cast on the FK value (ri_triggers.c). A role that can
19	# CREATE TYPE / FUNCTION / CAST and holds REFERENCES on another owner's table can
20	# therefore run its own SQL as that owner — reaching COPY ... TO PROGRAM if the owner
21	# has pg_execute_server_program. Unpatched upstream as of 2026-07-24.

23	# not shared with any untrusted party. Adding a second, less-trusted role to the

25	# this. See the guardrail row in docs/progress.md.

1	"""Request rate limiting on every public surface (#725, ADR 0035).
2	
3	One HTTP middleware, registered on the parent FastAPI app as the *innermost*
4	user middleware (see `backend/app/main.py`), so a 429 still exits through
5	CORSMiddleware (cross-origin browsers see the 429, not an opaque CORS error)
6	and through `request_id_middleware` (429s get `X-Request-ID` + the structured
7	request log). Being on the parent app — not a route dependency — is what lets it
8	also cover the mounted FastMCP sub-app at `/mcp`.
9	
10	Algorithm: a fixed-window counter (60s). The window index is baked *into* the
11	Redis key (`rl:{cls}:{key}:{window}`), so there is no read-modify-EXPIRE race —
12	the key simply changes at each window boundary, and EXPIRE is pure garbage
13	collection at 2x the window. Counting is one round-trip (INCR + EXPIRE pipeline).
14	
15	Fail-open: any store error → the request is allowed (a Redis outage disables
16	limiting, logged once per window — never a hard-down on the whole API).
17	
18	The `default` (bearer) class carries a dual-key ceiling: besides the per-token
19	bucket it also increments a per-IP `ipall` bucket counting ALL bearer traffic
20	from one IP, so an attacker rotating a fresh random `Bearer <nonce>` per request
21	(which would otherwise mint a fresh `tok:` bucket every time and never 429) is
22	still capped by `rate_limit_ip_per_minute`. The `webhook` class carries the same
23	dual-key shape (#785): its primary bucket is per provider + IP (so one noisy
24	orchestrator can't crowd out another's callbacks), and a per-IP `ipall` ceiling
25	(`rate_limit_webhook_ip_per_minute`) bounds the aggregate one IP can spend
26	across provider buckets. Both counters move in one pipelined round trip.
27	
28	"Per-IP" everywhere above means per address PREFIX (#789 — IPv4 /24, IPv6 /64
29	by default, configurable): keying on the full address lets a rotating NAT/proxy
30	pool spread a burst across sibling addresses so no bucket ever fills. See
31	`_bucket_ip`.
32	"""

288	def _strip_ipv4_port(host: str) -> str:
289	    match = _IPV4_PORT_RE.match(host)
290	    return match.group(1) if match else host
291	
292	
293	def _is_ip(value: str) -> bool:
294	    try:
295	        ipaddress.ip_address(value)
296	        return True
297	    except ValueError:
298	        return False
299	
300	
301	def _client_ip(request: Request, trusted_hops: int) -> str:
302	    """The client IP for per-IP buckets.
303	
304	    X-Forwarded-For is a comma-separated chain — each trusted proxy appends the
305	    peer it saw. Exactly `trusted_hops` proxies are trusted to append (config
306	    `RATE_LIMIT_XFF_TRUSTED_HOPS`), so the real client is the entry
307	    `trusted_hops` from the right (`entries[len - hops]`). Picking a fixed depth
308	    from the right is what survives a multi-proxy chain: a single-proxy compose
309	    setup uses hops=1 (rightmost), while the ACA public-envoy→nginx→internal-
310	    envoy chain uses hops=3.
311	
312	    If the chain is SHORTER than `trusted_hops`, the request did not traverse the
313	    expected proxy stack, so the whole XFF header is untrustworthy → fall back to
314	    the socket peer (never `entries[0]`, the most spoofable position). Whitespace
315	    is tolerated and an IPv4 `:port` suffix stripped; a garbage candidate or a
316	    missing peer falls back to `"unknown"`.
317	    """
318	    xff = request.headers.get("x-forwarded-for")
319	    if xff and trusted_hops >= 1:
320	        entries = [e.strip() for e in xff.split(",")]
321	        if len(entries) >= trusted_hops:
322	            candidate = _strip_ipv4_port(entries[len(entries) - trusted_hops])
323	            if candidate and _is_ip(candidate):
324	                return candidate
325	    client = request.client
326	    if client is not None and client.host:
327	        return client.host
328	    return "unknown"
329	
330	
331	def _bucket_ip(ip: str, settings: Settings) -> str:
332	    """The per-IP bucket key component: `ip` folded onto its address prefix (#789).
333	
334	    Keying per full /32 dilutes the cap against a rotating NAT/proxy pool — the
335	    pool spreads a burst across many sibling addresses so no single bucket ever
336	    fills (observed live: 200 requests over 11 distinct IPs in one /24, none near
337	    the cap). Folding onto a configurable prefix (IPv4 `rate_limit_ipv4_prefix`,
338	    default /24; IPv6 `rate_limit_ipv6_prefix`, default /64 — one subscriber's
339	    standard allocation) makes the whole pool share one bucket. The prefix length
340	    rides in the key, so retuning the mask starts fresh buckets rather than
341	    cross-counting. A non-address (`"unknown"`) passes through unchanged.
342	
343	    An IPv4-mapped IPv6 address (`::ffff:a.b.c.d` — what a dual-stack `[::]`
344	    listener's socket peer or a proxy-written XFF entry carries) is unwrapped and
345	    folded as IPv4: every mapped address lives in `::ffff:0:0/96`, so folding it
346	    at /64 would collapse the ENTIRE IPv4 internet into one `::/64` bucket — one
347	    abusive client would 429 all unauthenticated IPv4 traffic — and the same
348	    client would key differently as `a.b.c.d` vs `::ffff:a.b.c.d`.
349	    """
350	    try:
351	        addr = ipaddress.ip_address(ip)
352	    except ValueError:
353	        return ip
354	    if isinstance(addr, ipaddress.IPv6Address) and addr.ipv4_mapped is not None:
355	        addr = addr.ipv4_mapped
356	    prefix = (
357	        settings.rate_limit_ipv4_prefix if addr.version == 4 else settings.rate_limit_ipv6_prefix
358	    )
359	    return str(ipaddress.ip_network((addr, prefix), strict=False))
360	
361	
362	def _resolve_policy(
363	    path: str, bearer: str | None, ip: str, settings: Settings
364	) -> tuple[str, int, str]:
365	    """Resolve (class, per-minute limit, bucket key) for a request.
366	
367	    Order matters: the webhook (machine) path and the auth (OTP mint/verify)
368	    path are BOTH keyed per-IP EVEN when a bearer is present, checked before the
369	    bearer branch, so neither can be dodged by presenting a token. A known
370	    provider segment (adf/airflow/dbt) is folded into the webhook key so each
371	    provider gets an independent per-IP bucket (#785). Otherwise a bearer
372	    buckets per sha256(token) and the unauthenticated path per client-IP. The
373	    raw token is never used as a key — only its hash — so it is never logged or
374	    stored.
375	    """
376	    if path.startswith(_WEBHOOK_PREFIX):
377	        provider = path[len(_WEBHOOK_PREFIX) :].split("/", 1)[0]
378	        prefix = f"{provider}:" if provider in _WEBHOOK_PROVIDERS else ""
379	        return "webhook", settings.rate_limit_webhook_per_minute, f"{prefix}ip:{ip}"
380	    if path.startswith(_AUTH_PREFIX):
381	        return "auth", settings.rate_limit_auth_per_minute, f"ip:{ip}"
382	    if bearer is not None:
383	        digest = hashlib.sha256(bearer.encode()).hexdigest()[:32]
384	        return "default", settings.rate_limit_authenticated_per_minute, f"tok:{digest}"
385	    return "unauth", settings.rate_limit_unauthenticated_per_minute, f"ip:{ip}"
386	
387	
388	def _warn_store_unavailable_once(window: int, *, path: str, cls: str, key: str) -> None:
389	    global _store_unavailable_warned_window
390	    if _store_unavailable_warned_window == window:
391	        return
392	    _store_unavailable_warned_window = window
393	    # Path only (never request.url / query string), class, and key KIND (tok/ip) —
394	    # never the key value. The kind's value domain is pinned to {tok, ip} — a
395	    # provider-folded webhook key (`adf:ip:…`, #785) still reports "ip" so log
396	    # queries keyed on the documented domain keep matching.
397	    log.warning(
398	        "rate_limit_store_unavailable",
399	        path=path,
400	        rate_limit_class=cls,
401	        key_kind="tok" if key.startswith("tok:") else "ip",
402	    )
403	
404	
405	async def rate_limit_middleware(
406	    request: Request, call_next: Callable[[Request], Awaitable[Response]]
407	) -> Response:
408	    settings = get_settings()
409	    if not settings.rate_limit_enabled:
410	        return await call_next(request)
411	    # Only a GENUINE CORS preflight is exempt — OPTIONS carrying both Origin and
412	    # Access-Control-Request-Method. A bare OPTIONS is counted like any request.
413	    if (
414	        request.method == "OPTIONS"
415	        and "origin" in request.headers
416	        and "access-control-request-method" in request.headers
417	    ):
418	        return await call_next(request)
419	    path = request.url.path
420	    if path in _EXEMPT_PATHS:
421	        return await call_next(request)
422	
423	    bearer = _bearer_token(request)
424	    # Every per-IP key site (policy key + the ipall ceilings) uses the PREFIX
425	    # bucket (#789), so a NAT/proxy pool rotating sibling addresses can't dilute
426	    # the cap. The raw client address is never a key input past this point.
427	    ip = _bucket_ip(_client_ip(request, settings.rate_limit_xff_trusted_hops), settings)
428	    cls, limit, key = _resolve_policy(path, bearer, ip, settings)
429	
430	    now = int(_now())
431	    window = now // WINDOW_SECONDS
432	
433	    # The `default` (bearer) class gets a SECOND per-IP `ipall` bucket that counts
434	    # all bearer traffic from one IP, closing the rotated-token bypass (a fresh
435	    # random bearer mints a fresh tok bucket but shares the ipall ceiling). The
436	    # `webhook` class gets the same dual-key shape (#785): its primary bucket is
437	    # per provider + IP, so without an `ipall` ceiling one IP could spend
438	    # (providers + 1) x the webhook cap by rotating the segment. The unauth class
439	    # stays single-key — it is already per-IP on its one bucket.
440	    keys = [f"rl:{cls}:{key}:{window}"]
441	    if cls == "default":
442	        keys.append(f"rl:default:ipall:{ip}:{window}")
443	    elif cls == "webhook":
444	        keys.append(f"rl:webhook:ipall:{ip}:{window}")
445	    counts = await _active_store().incr_windows(keys)
446	
447	    if counts is None:
448	        # Fail-open: store unavailable → allow, warn once per window.
449	        _warn_store_unavailable_once(window, path=path, cls=cls, key=key)
450	        return await call_next(request)
451	
452	    # Primary bucket checked first so it wins the reported limit when both exceed.
453	    exceeded_limit: int | None = None
454	    if counts[0] > limit:
455	        exceeded_limit = limit
456	    elif cls == "default" and counts[1] > settings.rate_limit_ip_per_minute:
457	        exceeded_limit = settings.rate_limit_ip_per_minute
458	    elif cls == "webhook" and counts[1] > settings.rate_limit_webhook_ip_per_minute:
459	        exceeded_limit = settings.rate_limit_webhook_ip_per_minute
460	
461	    if exceeded_limit is not None:
462	        retry_after = max(1, (window + 1) * WINDOW_SECONDS - now)
463	        return JSONResponse(
464	            status_code=429,
465	            content=error_envelope(
466	                "rate_limited",
467	                "Too many requests",
468	                {"retry_after_seconds": retry_after},
469	            ),
470	            headers={
471	                "Retry-After": str(retry_after),
472	                "X-RateLimit-Limit": str(exceeded_limit),
473	                "X-RateLimit-Remaining": "0",
474	            },
475	        )
476	    return await call_next(request)

# returns None when MCP must not be exposed (no resolvable auth — see
# mcp.auth.mcp_enabled), so the endpoint never goes live unauthenticated. Its
# streamable-http session manager needs its lifespan run, so when present we
# combine it with the app's own startup (combine_lifespans, fastmcp docs).
_mcp_app = build_mcp_app()
_lifespan = combine_lifespans(lifespan, _mcp_app.lifespan) if _mcp_app is not None else lifespan


def docs_kwargs(settings: Settings) -> dict[str, str | None]:
    """FastAPI doc-exposure kwargs, gated by environment (#170 — prod-docs gate).

    The interactive docs (`/docs`, `/redoc`) and the raw OpenAPI schema
    (`/openapi.json`) are OFF in production — don't publish the full API surface
    on the public ingress — and ON in dev/staging for developer convenience.
    Disabling `openapi_url` also disables both doc UIs (they fetch it), so all
    three ride the one environment check.
    """
    enabled = settings.environment != "prod"
    return {
        "docs_url": "/docs" if enabled else None,
        "redoc_url": "/redoc" if enabled else None,
        "openapi_url": "/openapi.json" if enabled else None,
    }


_docs = docs_kwargs(get_settings())
app = FastAPI(
    title="DataQ API",
    lifespan=_lifespan,
    docs_url=_docs["docs_url"],
    redoc_url=_docs["redoc_url"],
    openapi_url=_docs["openapi_url"],
)

# Rate limiting (#725, ADR 0035). Registered FIRST → the INNERMOST user
# middleware, so a 429 still exits through CORSMiddleware (cross-origin browsers
# see the 429, not an opaque CORS error) and through request_id_middleware (429s
# get X-Request-ID + the structured request log). On the PARENT app so it also
# covers the mounted FastMCP sub-app at /mcp — a route dependency would not.
app.middleware("http")(rate_limit_middleware)

# Cross-origin access for the prod Static-Web-App ↔ Container-Apps split. Added
# only when origins are configured (empty in dev — the Vite proxy keeps it
# same-origin), so the allowlist is explicit and never `*`. credentials=True so
# the bearer/auth flow works from the SPA origin.
_cors_origins = get_settings().cors_allow_origin_list
if _cors_origins:
    app.add_middleware(
        CORSMiddleware,
        allow_origins=_cors_origins,
        allow_credentials=True,
        allow_methods=["*"],
        allow_headers=["*"],

        # allowlist — the browser drops any response header not listed here on a
        # cross-origin fetch, so a same-origin dev proxy can see it fine while a
        # cross-origin deploy (or the frontend's own axios client, generally)
        # would silently read `undefined` without this entry.
        expose_headers=[REQUEST_ID_HEADER, TOTAL_COUNT_HEADER],
    )

# by the backend's new provider-neutral `OidcBearerScheme` (ADR 0026
# amendment) instead of the Azure-only `fastapi_azure_auth` path. No code
# change needed here beyond what already shipped: this stack only needs to
# set OIDC_ISSUER + OIDC_AUDIENCE (backend) and the DATAQ_AUTH_* runtime
# contract (frontend, already generic per ADR 0028).
#
# Known open item (tracked, not silently assumed correct): Cognito's OAuth
# ACCESS token carries `client_id`, not the standard `aud` claim.
# OidcBearerScheme already accommodates this — see its docstring — but the
# accommodation needs confirming against a REAL token from this pool once
# it exists (this codebase's "#953 rule": driver/third-party-boundary claims
# need a live check, not just a spec read).

resource "aws_cognito_user_pool" "app" {
  name = "dataq-app"

  auto_verified_attributes = ["email"]

  password_policy {
    minimum_length    = 12
    require_lowercase = true
    require_numbers   = true
    require_symbols   = true
    require_uppercase = true
  }

  username_attributes = ["email"]

  tags = { Name = "dataq-app-cognito" }
}

# Domain prefix must be globally unique across all of Cognito — the random
# suffix (shared with other globally-unique-name resources in this stack)
# avoids a name collision on a common word like "dataq".
resource "aws_cognito_user_pool_domain" "app" {
  domain       = "dataq-app-${random_string.suffix.result}"
  user_pool_id = aws_cognito_user_pool.app.id
}

# Public SPA client — no secret (a browser can't hold one), matching how the
# frontend's oidc-client-ts uses Authorization Code + PKCE (authClient.ts).
resource "aws_cognito_user_pool_client" "spa" {
  name         = "dataq-app-spa"
  user_pool_id = aws_cognito_user_pool.app.id

  generate_secret = false

  allowed_oauth_flows_user_pool_client = true
  allowed_oauth_flows                  = ["code"]
  allowed_oauth_scopes                 = ["openid", "email", "profile"]
  supported_identity_providers         = ["COGNITO"]

  # Root-with-trailing-slash, matching what the SPA actually registers:
  # authClient.ts uses `redirect_uri: ${window.location.origin}/` (and the same
  # for post-logout) — it has no /auth/callback route. Cognito matches redirect
  # URIs exactly, so anything else is an instant redirect_mismatch (#1345).
  # HTTPS is mandatory here (Cognito rejects non-localhost http://) — satisfied
  # by fronting the ALB with CloudFront (cloudfront.tf).
  callback_urls = ["${local.frontend_url}/"]
  logout_urls   = ["${local.frontend_url}/"]

  # Access tokens are short-lived (1h) by default; the SPA relies on
  # oidc-client-ts's silent-renew via the refresh token, same pattern Azure
  # uses (authClient.ts requests offline_access).
  explicit_auth_flows = ["ALLOW_USER_SRP_AUTH", "ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH"]
}

  # exactly what OidcBearerScheme's `discover_jwks_uri` GETs
  # `{issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration` from.
  cognito_issuer = "https://cognito-idp.${var.aws_region}.amazonaws.com/${aws_cognito_user_pool.app.id}"
}

    claims: dict[str, Any] = azure_user.claims
    aad_oid = str(claims["oid"])
    email = str(claims.get("preferred_username") or claims.get("email") or claims.get("upn") or "")
    display_name_raw = claims.get("name")
    display_name = str(display_name_raw) if display_name_raw is not None else None

def _extract_oidc_claims(claims: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[str, str, str | None]:
    """The generic-OIDC counterpart to `_extract_claims`.

    `sub` — RFC 7519's REQUIRED subject claim — not Azure's non-standard `oid`;
    bare `claims["sub"]` on purpose, so a token missing it (a malformed/misissued
    token, since every compliant OIDC provider sets it) fails loudly rather than
    silently keying a row on an empty string.

    subject = str(claims["sub"])
    email = str(claims.get("email") or "")
    display_name_raw = claims.get("name")
    display_name = str(display_name_raw) if display_name_raw is not None else None

content.text:
I audited both stacks from the IaC and app code, then verified the important claims against the live deployments rather than trusting the docs.

## Verified good on both clouds

| Control | Azure | AWS | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Single public surface | frontend ACA only | CloudFront only | api direct → 404 (Azure), ALB direct → connection refused |
| Backend reachable directly? | No (internal ingress) | No (SG = CloudFront prefix list + origin secret) | probed both |
| DB reachable? | No | No | RDS resolves to `10.20.18.65`, `PubliclyAccessible: false`, encrypted |
| Redis reachable? | No (internal ACA + `requirepass`, pinned `redis:7`) | No (in-VPC, TLS + auth token) | SG/ingress scoped to task SG |
| Swagger/OpenAPI in prod | Off | Off | `/openapi.json` → `text/html` SPA shell; `ENVIRONMENT=prod` |
| Rate limiting enforcing | Yes | Yes | 150-req burst → **32× 429** (Azure), **60× 429** (AWS) |
| Webhook auth | HMAC-SHA256 / shared secret, `compare_digest` | same | [orchestration.py](backend/app/api/v1/orchestration.py) |
| Secrets | Key Vault via UAMI | Secrets Manager via task role | no bootstrap credential either side |

ECS tasks carry public IPs (no-NAT design), but I confirmed inbound is genuinely blocked — port 8000 on `3.15.137.1` times out; the SG has no `0.0.0.0/0` ingress.

## Findings

**P1 — AWS: anyone on the internet can get an authenticated DataQ account.** This is the one that matters.

The Cognito pool has `AllowAdminCreateUserOnly: false`, and I confirmed the hosted signup page serves a working form:

```
https://dataq-app-l4y8n8.auth.us-east-2.amazoncognito.com/signup?... → 200, <form>, Sign up
```

The backend has no allowlist on the generic-OIDC path — [auth.py:882-889](backend/app/core/auth.py#L882-L889) goes straight from valid token to `_upsert_user`. So: self-register → verify email → auto-provisioned DataQ user. MFA is `OFF`, advanced security is `null`.

**This chains with open issue [#1118](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/1118).** That issue's whole risk acceptance is "under the current single-tenant *workspace-trusted* model" — i.e. any authenticated user. Open signup dissolves that premise: an attacker self-registers, reads a victim connection's `catalog_secret_name` off `GET /connections`, then `POST /connections/test` with `catalog_uri` pointed at their own host → the server resolves the real warehouse credential and sends it to them. Deferred-to-RBAC becomes remotely exploitable.

Azure is **not** affected — the AAD tenant is the gate; guests must be invited.

Fix: `admin_create_user_config { allow_admin_create_user_only = true }` on the pool (one-line, immediate), plus an app-side signup allowlist on the OIDC path mirroring what OTP mode already has.

**P2 — No security response headers, either cloud.** Confirmed live: zero `Strict-Transport-Security`, `Content-Security-Policy`, `X-Frame-Options`, `X-Content-Type-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`. A repo-wide grep returns nothing. This matters more than usual here because the UI renders warehouse-supplied content (failing sample rows, error text) — no CSP is the missing backstop for an XSS in that path. Also `server: nginx/1.27.5` discloses the version. Fix is ~6 `add_header` lines in [nginx.conf.template](frontend/nginx.conf.template) + `server_tokens off`.

**P3 — ElastiCache at-rest encryption disabled** (`AtRestEncryptionEnabled: false`). TLS and auth token are on; `at_rest_encryption_enabled` is simply absent from [elasticache.tf](deploy/terraform/aws/elasticache.tf). Free to enable, requires replacement.

**P4 — Azure Postgres is on the shared server behind allow-all-Azure-services.** Any resource in any Azure tenant can reach it at network level; only credentials stop them. AWS's SG-scoped RDS is materially stricter. Noted in [postgres.tf](deploy/terraform/azure/postgres.tf) as a shared-server consequence.

**P5 — Unrestricted egress on both.** ECS tasks and ACA apps can reach anything outbound. That's the exfiltration path for P1/#1118, and nothing constrains it.

## Attack-class assessment

**DDoS** — the weakest area. CloudFront gives Shield Standard for L3/L4, but it's configured `Managed-CachingDisabled`, so it's a pure pass-through: **every** request reaches the origin and it absorbs nothing at L7. Behind it sits `desired_count = 1` on all three services with no autoscaling. Azure is worse — no Front Door/WAF, ACA scales api to max 3 and worker is pinned at 1. Neither cloud has a WAF. And the app rate limiter **fails open** by design (ADR 0035 chooses availability), with a 5s breaker — so a flood that also stresses Redis switches limiting off precisely when it's needed. Containment: add AWS WAF with rate-based rules on the distribution, cache static assets at the edge, enable ECS/ACA autoscaling, and put Azure behind Front Door + WAF.

**Fuzzing** — the strongest area. Pydantic validation throughout, an explicit NUL-byte rejection middleware, a structured error envelope, an adversarial-input harness in `tests/support/`, and the go-live workout that hit 21 injection points with zero 500s. Residual: authenticated custom-SQL is a deliberate feature, so input hardening isn't the boundary there — authz is, which loops back to P1.

**MITM** — TLS to both edges. Two soft spots, both documented: the CloudFront→ALB hop is plain HTTP (no custom domain, so no ACM cert the ALB could serve), meaning the origin secret and all session traffic transit that leg in cleartext; and no HSTS anywhere, so a first-visit downgrade isn't blocked. Fix is the same one thing — custom domain + ACM on the ALB + `https-only`.

**Replay** — the HMAC webhooks have no timestamp or nonce, so a captured signed body can be replayed to re-ingest an event and potentially re-trigger a suite run. Bounded (the trigger-dedup index from #456 limits the damage), but it's a free resource-consumption vector.

1. Close Cognito self-signup — today. It's one Terraform line and it's the difference between #1118 being an accepted internal risk and a remote credential-exfiltration bug.
2. Add the security headers to nginx — one file, both clouds.
3. AWS WAF rate-based rule on the distribution + edge caching for `/assets/*`.
4. Custom domain + ACM, which closes the cleartext origin hop and lets you set HSTS meaningfully.
5. ElastiCache at-rest encryption; egress restrictions.

def _oidc_access_allowed(email: str) -> bool:
    """Whether `email` (already normalized) may hold a DataQ account via OIDC (#1385).

    Mirrors `otp_service.is_signup_eligible`, with one deliberate difference in the
    empty-allowlist case: OTP treats "no allowlist" as *nobody* (and refuses to
    boot), while this returns True — see the `oidc_allowed_emails` field comment
    in `core/config.py` for why a fail-closed default here would turn a routine
    image bump into a workspace-wide lockout.

    Checked on EVERY request, not only at first provisioning. Gating just the
    insert would leave an already-provisioned identity in place after it is
    removed from the allowlist, so the list would grant access but never revoke
    it — this way it doubles as the kill-switch for an account that should no
    longer be admitted.
    """
    settings = get_settings()
    if not settings.oidc_allowlist_configured:
        return True
    if email in settings.oidc_allowed_email_set:
        return True
    _, _, domain = email.partition("@")
    return bool(domain) and domain in settings.oidc_allowed_domain_set


def _resolve_generic_oidc_user(db: Session, oidc_claims: dict[str, Any]) -> User:
    """Claims -> allowlist gate -> upserted `User`, for both generic-OIDC deps.

    Deliberately ONE function called from both `_get_current_user_generic_oidc`
    and `_get_current_user_generic_oidc_or_otp`: the two dependencies had byte-
    identical bodies here, and a gate added to one and forgotten in the other
    would leave the mode that also has OTP enabled silently ungated.
    """
    subject, email, display_name = _extract_oidc_claims(oidc_claims)
    email = normalize_email(email)
    if not _oidc_access_allowed(email):
        # Deliberately 403, not 401: the token is VALID: re-authenticating would
        # loop the SPA forever. The address is not echoed back — the caller
        # already knows who they signed in as, and the log line below is where an
        # operator reads it.
        log.warning("auth_oidc_access_denied", mode="generic_oidc", email=email)
        raise DataQError(
            code="forbidden",
            message="This account is not authorized for this DataQ workspace.",
            status_code=403,
        )
    user = _upsert_user(
        db,
        aad_object_id=subject,
        email=email,
        display_name=display_name,
        oidc_issuer=_settings.oidc_issuer,
    )
    log.info("auth_user_resolved", mode="generic_oidc", user_id=str(user.id))
    return user


def _get_current_user_generic_oidc(
    request: Request,
    oidc_claims: Annotated[dict[str, Any] | None, Security(oidc_scheme)],

) -> User:

resource "aws_cognito_user_pool" "app" {
  name = "dataq-app"

  auto_verified_attributes = ["email"]

  # NO self-service sign-up (#1385). This is the load-bearing line in this file.
  #
  # A Cognito pool allows self-registration by DEFAULT, and the hosted UI serves
  # a working /signup form to anyone who finds the domain. DataQ auto-provisions
  # a user row for any identity the configured issuer vouches for
  # (`core/auth.py`'s `_upsert_user`), so the pool's registration policy IS the
  # product's access policy: with sign-up open, any stranger could register,
  # verify their own email, and land an authenticated account inside the
  # workspace. That also dissolved the "single-tenant, workspace-trusted"
  # premise that issue #1118 (arbitrary `*_secret_name` resolution -> warehouse-
  # credential exfiltration) is deliberately accepted under, turning a known
  # internal risk into a remotely reachable one.
  #
  # With this set, operators are created by an admin
  # (`aws cognito-idp admin-create-user`) and the hosted /signup endpoint stops
  # serving a form. Existing users are unaffected.
  admin_create_user_config {
    allow_admin_create_user_only = true
  }

    with pytest.raises(DataQError) as excinfo:
        auth_mod._get_current_user_generic_oidc(_request(), None, db_session)

# ── OIDC access allowlist (#1385) ────────────────────────────────────────────
# The defect being pinned: a valid token from the issuer was sufficient to be
# auto-provisioned a DataQ account, so a self-signup-enabled IdP (the AWS
# Cognito pool, as shipped) let anyone on the internet in.

# Both generic-OIDC dependencies must be gated. They had byte-identical bodies,
# so a gate added to one and missed on the other is the realistic regression —
# hence parametrizing over both rather than testing the primary one twice.
_OIDC_DEPS = pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "dependency",
    [auth_mod._get_current_user_generic_oidc, auth_mod._get_current_user_generic_oidc_or_otp],
    ids=["generic_oidc", "generic_oidc_or_otp"],
)


@_OIDC_DEPS
def test_oidc_allowlist_denies_an_address_not_on_it(
    db_session: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, dependency: Any
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        auth_mod, "_settings", _oidc_settings(oidc_allowed_emails="invited@example.com")
    )
    with pytest.raises(DataQError) as excinfo:
        dependency(
            _request(),
            _oidc_claims({"sub": "stranger-sub", "email": "stranger@evil.test"}),
            db_session,
        )
    # 403, not 401: the token is valid, so re-authenticating would loop forever.
    assert excinfo.value.status_code == 403
    assert excinfo.value.code == "forbidden"


@_OIDC_DEPS
def test_oidc_allowlist_denial_provisions_no_user_row(
    db_session: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, dependency: Any
) -> None:
    """The point of the gate is that the row never appears — a 403 that still
    inserted would leave the account behind for any later path to resolve."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        auth_mod, "_settings", _oidc_settings(oidc_allowed_domains="example.com")
    )
    with pytest.raises(DataQError):
        dependency(
            _request(),
            _oidc_claims({"sub": "no-row-sub", "email": "nobody@evil.test"}),
            db_session,
        )
    assert (
        db_session.query(User).filter(User.aad_object_id == "no-row-sub").one_or_none() is None
    )


@_OIDC_DEPS
def test_oidc_allowlist_admits_a_listed_address(
    db_session: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, dependency: Any
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        auth_mod, "_settings", _oidc_settings(oidc_allowed_emails="invited@example.com")
    )
    user = dependency(
        _request(),
        _oidc_claims({"sub": f"invited-{dependency.__name__}", "email": "invited@example.com"}),
        db_session,
    )
    assert user.email == "invited@example.com"


def test_oidc_allowlist_admits_a_listed_domain(
    db_session: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(auth_mod, "_settings", _oidc_settings(oidc_allowed_domains="example.com"))
    user = auth_mod._get_current_user_generic_oidc(
        _request(),
        _oidc_claims({"sub": "domain-sub", "email": "anyone@example.com"}),
        db_session,
    )
    assert user.email == "anyone@example.com"


def test_oidc_allowlist_matches_case_insensitively_and_ignores_surrounding_space(
    db_session: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """The allowlist and the token must normalize identically, or a capitalised
    claim silently reads as ineligible against a lower-cased list."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        auth_mod, "_settings", _oidc_settings(oidc_allowed_emails=" Invited@Example.COM , x@y.z ")
    )
    user = auth_mod._get_current_user_generic_oidc(
        _request(),
        _oidc_claims({"sub": "case-sub", "email": "INVITED@example.com"}),
        db_session,
    )
    assert user.email == "invited@example.com"


def test_oidc_allowlist_tolerates_an_at_prefixed_domain_entry(
    db_session: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """`@acme.io` is what an operator naturally writes; if it did not match, the
    allowlist would reject everyone while looking correctly configured."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(auth_mod, "_settings", _oidc_settings(oidc_allowed_domains="@example.com"))
    user = auth_mod._get_current_user_generic_oidc(
        _request(),
        _oidc_claims({"sub": "at-domain-sub", "email": "someone@example.com"}),
        db_session,
    )
    assert user.email == "someone@example.com"


def test_oidc_allowlist_unset_admits_everyone(
    db_session: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """The documented default. Fail-OPEN here is deliberate (a fail-closed default
    would lock an existing workspace out on a routine image bump) — pinned so the
    default can never be flipped silently in either direction."""
    settings = _oidc_settings()
    assert settings.oidc_allowlist_configured is False
    monkeypatch.setattr(auth_mod, "_settings", settings)
    user = auth_mod._get_current_user_generic_oidc(
        _request(),
        _oidc_claims({"sub": "ungated-sub", "email": "anyone@anywhere.test"}),
        db_session,
    )
    assert user.email == "anyone@anywhere.test"


def test_oidc_allowlist_revokes_an_already_provisioned_user(
    db_session: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """Gating only the INSERT would let an identity provisioned while the list was
    open keep its access forever — the list would grant but never revoke."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(auth_mod, "_settings", _oidc_settings())
    existing = auth_mod._get_current_user_generic_oidc(
        _request(),
        _oidc_claims({"sub": "revoked-sub", "email": "former@evil.test"}),
        db_session,
    )
    assert existing.id is not None

    monkeypatch.setattr(
        auth_mod, "_settings", _oidc_settings(oidc_allowed_domains="example.com")
    )
    with pytest.raises(DataQError) as excinfo:
        auth_mod._get_current_user_generic_oidc(
            _request(),
            _oidc_claims({"sub": "revoked-sub", "email": "former@evil.test"}),
            db_session,
        )
    assert excinfo.value.status_code == 403


def test_oidc_allowlist_denies_a_token_carrying_no_email(
    db_session: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """Cognito access tokens carry no `email` — it is filled from the userinfo
    endpoint (#1346). If that round-trip fails the claim is empty, and an empty
    address must not slip past a configured allowlist."""
    monkeypatch.setattr(auth_mod, "_settings", _oidc_settings(oidc_allowed_domains="example.com"))
    with pytest.raises(DataQError) as excinfo:
        auth_mod._get_current_user_generic_oidc(
            _request(), _oidc_claims({"sub": "no-email-sub"}), db_session
        )
    assert excinfo.value.status_code == 403


def test_oidc_allowlist_does_not_gate_pat_authentication(
    db_session: Any, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    """A PAT is resolved before any OIDC claim exists, so the gate must not reach
    it — otherwise turning the allowlist on would break every MCP/API client."""
    user, token = _user_with_pat(db_session)
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        auth_mod, "_settings", _oidc_settings(oidc_allowed_emails="someone-else@example.com")
    )
    resolved = auth_mod._get_current_user_generic_oidc(
        _request(f"Bearer {token}"), None, db_session
    )
    assert resolved.id == user.id
